<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par53" />Of a different kind are the ''denominatives'' from: {{GHGheb|text=אזן}} (scarcely ''to prick up the ears'', but) ''to act with the ears, to hear''; cf. {{GHGheb|text=לשׁן|translate=to move the tongue, to slander}}, and the German ''äugeln'' (to make eyes), ''füsseln, näseln, schwänzeln''; {{GHGheb|text=שׁבר|translate=to sell corn}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁכם|translate=to set out early}} (to load the back [of the camel, &c.]?); opposed to {{GHGheb|text=הֶֽעֱרִיב}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|h}}
'''3.''' The meaning of {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} is (''a'') primarily that of a {{GHGterm|passive}} of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁלִיךְ|translate=proiecit}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָשְׁלַךְ}} or {{GHGheb|text=הֻשְׁלַךְ|translate=proiectus est}}; (''b'') sometimes equivalent to a passive of {{GHGterm|Qal}}, as {{GHGheb|text=נָקַם|translate=to avenge}}, Hoph. ''to be avenged'' (but see below, u).

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|i}}
Rem. 1. The ''î'' of the 3rd sing. masc. perf. {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} remains, without exception, in the 3rd fem. (in the tone-syllable). That it was, however, only lengthened from a short vowel, and consequently is changeable, is proved by the forms of the {{GHGterm|imperative}} and {{GHGterm|imperfect}} where ''ē'' (or, under the influence of gutturals, ''ă'') takes its place. In an open syllable the ''î'' is retained almost throughout; only in very isolated instances has it been weakened to {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} (see n and o).

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|k}}
2. The {{GHGterm|infinitive absolute}} commonly has {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} without ''Yodh'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַקְדֵּשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=17|verse=3}}; less frequently it takes {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַשְׁמֵיד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=9|verse=8}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=15|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=32|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=34|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=10|verse=10}}. With {{GHGheb|text=א}} instead of {{GHGheb|text=ה}} (probably a mere scribal error, not an Aramaism) we find {{GHGheb|text=אַשְׁכֵּים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=3}}. Rare exceptions, where the form with {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} stands for the {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}}, are, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=8}} (Sam. {{GHGheb|text=בְּהַנְחִיל}}; read perhaps {{GHGheb|text=בְּהַנְחִל}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=19.25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=25|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=3}} (?); on the other hand, for {{GHGheb|text=לַעְשֵׂר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=26|verse=12}} (which looks like an infinitive Hiphʿîl with elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, for {{GHGheb|text=לְהַֽעֲשִׂיר}}) the right reading is simply {{GHGheb|text=לְעַשֵּׂר}}, since elsewhere the Piʿēl alone occurs with the meaning ''to tithe''; for {{GHGheb|text=בַּעְשֵׂר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=10|verse=39}} perhaps the inf. Qal ({{GHGheb|text=בַּעְשׂר}}) was intended, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=8|verse=15.17}} (=''to take the tithe''). At the same time it is doubtful whether the present punctuation does not arise from a conflation of two different readings, the Qal and the Piʿēl.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|l}}
Instead of the ordinary form of the {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטִיל}} the form {{GHGheb|text=הִקְטִיל}} sometimes occurs, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁמִיד|translate=to destroy}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=48|hidebook=1}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=14|verse=46}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=11|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=33|hidebook=1}} and {{GHGheb|text=הִקְצוֹת}} for {{GHGheb|text=הַקְצוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=14|verse=43}} from {{GHGheb|text=קָצָה}}; scarcely, however, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=7|verse=35}} (see {{GHGpar|155|l}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=1}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=1}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=16}} (after {{GHGheb|text=עַד}}), and in the passages so explained by König (i. 276) where {{GHGheb|text=הִשְׁאִיר}} appears after prepositions<ref>As to the doubtfulness, on general grounds, of this form of the Inf. Hiph., see Robertson Smith in the {{GHGcite|title=Journ. of Philol.}}, xvi. p. 72 f.</ref>; [cf. Driver on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=7|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=55|hidebook=1}}].

With ''ă'' in the second syllable there occurs {{GHGheb|text=הַזְכַּרְכֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=29}} (cf. the substantival infin. {{GHGheb|text=הַפְצַ֑ר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=23}}).—In the Aram. manner {{GHGheb|text=לְהַשְׁמָעוּת}} is found in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=24|verse=26}} (as a construct form) for the {{GHGterm|infinitive Hiphʿîl}} (cf. the {{GHGterm|infinitive Hithpa‛el}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=11|verse=23}}). On the elision of the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} after prefixes, see q.

{{GHGmargin-letter|53|m}}
3. In the {{GHGterm|imperative}} the ''î'' is retained throughout in the open syllable, according to ''i'', and consequently also before suffixes (see {{GHGpar|61|g}}) and {{GHGheb|text=־ָה|translate=paragogic}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַקְשִׁ֫יבָה|translate=attend to}}, {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשִׁ֫יעָה נָּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=25}}, as in ed. Mant., Jabl., Baer, not {{GHGheb|text=הוֹשִׁיעָ֫ה נָּא}} as Ginsb. and Kittel; with the tone at the end only {{GHGheb|text=הַצְלִיחָה}} ibid. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=25b|hidebook=v}}. On the other hand, in the 2nd sing. masc. the original ''ĭ'' (cf. Arabic ''ʾáqtĭl'') is lengthened to ''ē'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַשְׁמֵן|translate=make fat}}, and becomes ''S<sup>e</sup>ghôl'' before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַסְכֶּן־נָא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=21}}.—The form {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטִיל}} for {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטֵל}} appears anomalously a few times: {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=94|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=18}} (cf. {{GHGpar|69|v}} and {{GHGpar|72|y}}); elsewhere the Masora has preferred the punctuation {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטֵיל}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=6}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=142|verse=5}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=5|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=הַבִּ֫יטָה}} is required by the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} for {{GHGheb|text=הביט}}.<section end="par53" /><noinclude>
